title: Her Kind of Surgery
teaser: Mido is already waiting beside the operating table for her first assistant.

choices.choice_em1_b1_a: Place a warm saline laparotomy pad half a beat early and gently pack the duodenum inferomedially.
choices.choice_em1_b1_b: Take the deep abdominal wall retractor and draw the right costal margin and inferior liver edge steadily upward.
choices.choice_em1_b1_c: Use atraumatic forceps on the opposite edge to create a fine counter-traction plane as Mido frees the omental adhesions.
choices.choice_em1_c1_a: "Pulling superolaterally crowds the neck. Let's retract inferolaterally instead—if you confirm, I'll adjust the angle."
choices.choice_em1_c1_b: "Hold off going deeper for now. Let me blot the surface ooze with a peanut sponge to clear the superficial margin first."
choices.choice_em1_c1_c: "Current traction is folding the neck. Should I open it inferolaterally, or steady the liver edge for you first?"
choices.choice_em1_e1_a: Skip the small talk, take the instruments, and begin closing steadily.
choices.choice_em1_e1_b: "Once I'm done, what score are you planning to give today's test, Chief Mido?"
choices.choice_em1_e1_c: "Looks like today's 'test' has finally reached the part where I hand in my paper."

nodes.em1_001: Some time after that brief, razor-edged meeting in her office, an assignment personally requested by the Chief Surgeon finally appeared on the surgical schedule board.
nodes.em1_002: —Elective open cholecystectomy. Primary Surgeon: Emiko Mido. First Assistant: Ryuji Sakaguchi.
nodes.em1_003: With several minutes still left before the scheduled start time, Ryuji Sakaguchi—fresh from a standard surgical scrub—held both hands raised before his chest, stepped over the foot sensor beside the door, and walked through the sliding entrance of Operating Room 1.
nodes.em1_004: The shadowless lamp was already on.
nodes.em1_005: Emiko Mido was already standing at the primary surgeon's position, her surgical cap, tie-on mask, long-sleeved sterile gown, and double latex gloves immaculate without a single crease. Behind the instrument table, Hiroko Sugimura had finished laying out the entire open biliary set in order; spotting Sakaguchi enter, she wordlessly readied a sterile hand towel and held open a sterile gown.
nodes.em1_006: Standing beside the operating table, Mido didn't even turn her head.
nodes.em1_008: Sakaguchi took the sterile towel to dry his hands, slipped his arms into the sleeves of the gown Hiroko held open while Moe Honjo stepped over from the circulating side to tie the back strings, then eased into the sterile gloves Hiroko offered and glanced up at the wall clock.
nodes.em1_009: "Still eight minutes before scheduled skin incision—are you timing this by a watch of your own?"
nodes.em1_010: "Someone in an operating room ought to keep time."
nodes.em1_011: That cool, clipped sentence instantly pulled the air across the entire room taut.
nodes.em1_012: At the center of the table, the thirty-six-year-old female patient remained awake under epidural anesthesia. Beyond the sterile ether screen at the head end, Moe Honjo had returned to the ECG monitor and was quietly verifying the blood pressure cuff and IV drip rate.
nodes.em1_013: Hearing the primary surgeon's voice, the patient spoke up from behind the drape, her voice slightly strained.
nodes.em1_014: "Dr. Mido... once you start operating, am I really going to stay awake the whole time?"
nodes.em1_017: "We already tested the epidural block level just now—incising the skin won't hurt. Being scared doesn't affect the operation itself."
nodes.em1_018: Standing at the head of the table, Moe Honjo blinked, glanced down at the patient's fingers clutching the edge of the sheet, and gathered her nerve to murmur softly through her mask:
nodes.em1_019: "Um, Dr. Mido... the patient hasn't done anything wrong. Anyone lying here for the first time is bound to feel scared..."
nodes.em1_020: Emiko Mido's hands paused for one second along the edge of the sterile drape.
nodes.em1_021: She lifted her eyes past the anesthesia frame toward the other side of the curtain. Her tone still held zero gentle inflection, yet she laid out the stakes with crystal clarity:
nodes.em1_022: "I'm keeping you awake not to torment you."
nodes.em1_023: "Epidural anesthesia interferes less with breathing and recovery; more importantly, you can answer questions at any moment. The instant deep traction causes chest tightness or any change in how you feel, I'll know right away."
nodes.em1_024: She tilted her chin ever so slightly toward Moe Honjo standing guard at the head end.
nodes.em1_027: "Mine is to perform the surgery properly."
nodes.em1_028: After half a second of quiet at the head of the table, Moe Honjo quickly took the back of the patient's hand resting on the armboard and spoke warmly:
nodes.em1_029: "Don't worry—I'll be right here beside your ear the whole time. Whenever anything feels uncomfortable, just give my hand a squeeze."
nodes.em1_030: The breathing behind the sterile screen gradually steadied.
nodes.em1_031: "...All right. Then I'm in your hands, Dr. Mido."
nodes.em1_032: From the first assistant's side across the table, Ryuji Sakaguchi studied the woman opposite him and formed his first firsthand impression—it wasn't that Emiko Mido failed to notice a patient's anxiety; she simply held the unyielding conviction that the greatest reassurance a primary surgeon could offer was a scalpel that never erred.
nodes.em1_033: "Patient name confirmed—thirty-six-year-old female, chronic calculous cholecystitis scheduled for open cholecystectomy; epidural block level and preoperative medications verified."
nodes.em1_034: Emiko Mido finally raised her eyelids, looking straight across the narrow operating table at Ryuji Sakaguchi.
nodes.em1_038: "I don't need you proving how clever you are at the table."
nodes.em1_041: "If you think that's simple, manage it first before saying so."
nodes.em1_042: The instant the words fell, she extended her right hand level toward the instrument stand:
nodes.em1_045: The blade came down cleanly along the marked right subcostal oblique incision line.
nodes.em1_046: Within the first two minutes alone, Ryuji Sakaguchi understood exactly where the hospital's rumors about its young Chief Surgeon came from.
nodes.em1_047: There wasn't a trace of tentative probing or repeated touch-ups in Emiko Mido's stroke—she carried the cut through skin and subcutaneous fat to the exact depth in a single pass, exposing the anterior rectus sheath cleanly; the moment two pinpoint bleeders welled up in the subcutis, the tip of her electrocautery forceps touched them with pinpoint precision, leaving neither blackened tissue from broad charring nor half a second of sluggish pause.
nodes.em1_048: Beside the Mayo stand, Hiroko Sugimura was plainly long accustomed to this razor-sharp tempo. Often the instant Mido angled her wrist a fraction, Metzenbaum scissors or a right-angle retractor had already landed squarely in her palm.
nodes.em1_049: The peritoneum opened smoothly, revealing the dark crimson inferior edge of the liver and the tense, mildly distended fundus of the gallbladder beneath the shadowless light.
nodes.em1_050: "No free fluid in the peritoneal cavity. Pack the transverse colon and duodenum inferomedially first and open up the subhepatic space."
nodes.em1_051: Even as she spoke, her left hand had already grasped and elevated the gallbladder fundus with atraumatic ring forceps, moving so briskly she barely left her assistant room to think.
nodes.em1_052: Without waiting for Mido to ask for a pad, Sakaguchi had already taken a folded, warm saline laparotomy sponge from Hiroko Sugimura. Sliding his left hand smoothly along the subhepatic space, he gently yet securely packed the duodenal bulb and hepatic flexure inferomedially while his right-hand suction tip skimmed the back of the pad to clear a trace of serous fluid, opening a wide, pristine working plane right in front of her.
nodes.em1_053: Mido's instrument glided into the space without a hitch, her eyelids lifting by half a millimeter:
nodes.em1_054: "...Your hands aren't slow. Hold that pad right where it is."
nodes.em1_055: Once the lower bowel had been packed away beneath a warm saline laparotomy pad, Sakaguchi took the S-shaped deep retractor steadily in both hands from Hiroko Sugimura, slid it gently beneath the inferior liver margin along the upper lip of the incision, and drew upward and laterally with even wrist tension. Even held suspended under traction, the blade tip didn't waver a hair beneath the shadowless lamp—no tremor, no slippage.
nodes.em1_056: Mido glanced over the suddenly wide-open right subhepatic vault without slowing her dissection for an instant:
nodes.em1_057: "Steady retractor. Keep that exact angle—don't ease off."
nodes.em1_058: Once the warm saline laparotomy pad was settled neatly over the duodenum, a band of adherent greater omentum showed along the rim of the gallbladder fundus. In the exact second Mido switched to tissue scissors, Sakaguchi's atraumatic tissue forceps caught the opposite edge of the omentum and drew out a translucent, fan-shaped plane of counter-traction.
nodes.em1_059: With a crisp snip, Mido divided the avascular plane cleanly in one stroke without shedding an extra drop of blood.
nodes.em1_060: "At least you can read where the primary surgeon intends to cut next second. Keep moving down."
nodes.em1_061: Less than ten minutes from skin incision—through entering the abdomen, packing off the bowel with a warm moist pad in the subhepatic space, and exposing the body of the gallbladder—two pairs of hands had crossed back and forth above the narrow incision without a single clash of instruments.
nodes.em1_062: Between instrument exchanges at the Mayo stand, Hiroko Sugimura's eyes curved almost imperceptibly above her mask—plainly, it had been a long while since a new partner kept pace with the Chief Surgeon on their very first case together.
nodes.em1_063: Continuing deeper along the body of the gallbladder, the operation entered the most critical—and least forgiving—zone of an open cholecystectomy: the transition from the gallbladder neck to the cystic duct and cystic artery.
nodes.em1_064: Yet as Emiko Mido used fine forceps to lift the thickened superficial peritoneum over the neck, her fluid forward tempo slowed for the first time.
nodes.em1_065: Because the patient had suffered repeated bouts of mild chronic cholecystitis, the serosa over the infundibular pouch at the gallbladder neck was thicker than preoperative ultrasound had suggested, with several dense inflammatory strands tethering the lower rim of the neck to the posteromedial tissue; the moment the loose superficial fascia was teased open, fine dark-red capillary beads welled along the raw edge, and under standard superolateral traction, the true boundary where the deep structures entered the gallbladder looked momentarily indistinct.
nodes.em1_066: A surgeon eager to show off might already have pushed a right-angle clamp bluntly deeper along the approximate line.
nodes.em1_067: Instead, Emiko Mido—who had been moving like wind seconds earlier—stopped her wrist dead in its tracks two millimeters short of the fascia.
nodes.em1_069: No bravado, and certainly no blind clamping while anatomical relationships remained unclear.
nodes.em1_070: Keeping her left hand rock-steady on the clamp, she lifted those cool, unruffled eyes straight toward the first assistant across from her:
nodes.em1_072: That wasn't a call for help—it was an uncompromising on-the-spot examination.
nodes.em1_073: Ryuji Sakaguchi leaned slightly forward over the deep operative field, his gaze sweeping rapidly across the obstructed focal point:
nodes.em1_074: "There's chronic inflammatory adhesion around Hartmann's pouch at the gallbladder neck, and the loose layer you just opened is still oozing into the serosal folds, obscuring the true margin where the ductal structures enter the gallbladder—it isn't safe to pass a clamp right now."
nodes.em1_075: Mido's gaze sharpened ever so slightly.
nodes.em1_077: "Continuing to pull superolaterally only bunches the sub-neck structures and posteromedial folds tighter together. If I take an atraumatic grasper on the infundibular pouch and draw it inferolaterally instead, setting up counter-traction against the inferior liver edge, that folded serosal plane will open right out—if you confirm, I'll adjust it now."
nodes.em1_078: Mido studied the field for a beat, then gave a crisp nod:
nodes.em1_079: "Your read isn't off. Retract along the vector you just described—slowly, so I can watch the deep tension."
nodes.em1_081: Taking the atraumatic grasping forceps from Hiroko Sugimura, Sakaguchi secured the lateral wall of the gallbladder neck; keeping a close eye on tension across the deep fascia, he rotated his wrist smoothly inferolaterally until the fold just flattened out, blotting away the surface ooze with a peanut sponge at the same time. The crowded lateral space beneath the neck opened by a clean layer, creating a clear entry for fine identification.
nodes.em1_082: "...Right vector. Hold that exact tension—don't add any more force."
nodes.em1_083: "Pushing deeper while the fascia is stained red with capillary ooze is the easiest way to misjudge a duct wall. Let's pause dissection for half a minute while I press the superficial bleeders dry with a warm saline peanut sponge and ease the neck slightly inferolaterally, so we expose a clean superficial contour free of bloodstain first."
nodes.em1_084: Mido glanced up at Sakaguchi, the faintest trace of approval crossing her cool gaze:
nodes.em1_085: "Just like what you wrote in your own operative note—you know when not to chase speed. Hiroko, peanut sponge for him."
nodes.em1_087: Sakaguchi picked up the warm, moist peanut sponge, pressed gently and accurately over the oozing fascial plane to blot the surface blood, and eased the gallbladder neck modestly inferolaterally, halting right where tissue tension settled evenly. When the sponge lifted away, the unstained superficial serosal fold at the neck stood out far more clearly, revealing the fibrous strands waiting underneath.
nodes.em1_088: "Much cleaner field. Maintain that exact hand pressure."
nodes.em1_089: "The current line of traction is folding the space beneath the neck shut. Would you like me to switch to an atraumatic grasper and open the gallbladder neck inferolaterally, or steady the deep liver retractor and blot the surface ooze for you first?"
nodes.em1_090: Concise and direct—pinpointing the cause of the obstructed view while leaving the final call squarely with the primary surgeon.
nodes.em1_091: "Have Hiroko lend a hand on the liver-edge retractor. Switch to an atraumatic grasper, draw the gallbladder neck inferolaterally nice and slow until the superficial fold flattens out, and blot away that surface ooze while you're at it."
nodes.em1_093: Switching to atraumatic grasping forceps, Sakaguchi kept close watch on the deep tissue tension as he eased the gallbladder neck smoothly inferolaterally, locking his wrist the instant the superficial fold flattened without tugging the deeper structures, while his other hand briskly wiped away the residual blood with a peanut sponge. The cramped lateral view around the neck opened up at once.
nodes.em1_094: "Exact right measure. An assistant who knows when to ask and where to stop his hand saves me plenty of breath."
nodes.em1_095: Sorting out exposure and tension was only step one; the real fine dissection was just beginning.
nodes.em1_096: While Sakaguchi held steady counter-traction on the grasper, Emiko Mido took a peanut sponge and fine dissecting forceps—not chasing recklessly deeper toward the common hepatic duct junction, but staying strictly flush against the wall of the gallbladder neck as she bluntly brushed back and divided the remaining strands of chronic inflammatory fibrous membrane layer by layer.
nodes.em1_097: Each time Mido teased aside a band obstructing the view, Sakaguchi's wrist micro-adjusted a degree along the newly opened cleft—never overstepping, yet keeping the working window flat and tension-free throughout. Within two minutes, the loose tissue immediately behind the gallbladder neck had been cleared into a clean, translucent safety window, isolating the tubular structures entering the gallbladder wall in crisp relief.
nodes.em1_098: Rather than placing clamps immediately, Mido touched the tip of her dissecting forceps lightly beneath the neck for one final two-surgeon verification:
nodes.em1_099: "No need to chase any deeper. Staying right along the gallbladder neck, reconfirm the two structures we're about to take."
nodes.em1_100: "This anterolateral structure continuing directly off the gallbladder neck is the cystic duct; this fine pulsating posteromedial branch entering straight into the gallbladder wall is the cystic artery. The space behind the neck is completely cleared, the surrounding safety margins are distinct, and no other tubular structure runs into the gallbladder."
nodes.em1_103: From that moment on, the rhythm across the entire operating table underwent a subtle yet unmistakable shift.
nodes.em1_104: Mido's spoken commands pared down from full sentences to minimal shorthand—
nodes.em1_106: Before the first syllable had scarcely left her lips, Sakaguchi's suction tip had already skimmed the margin to clear a trace of fluid without blocking her line of sight for an instant.
nodes.em1_108: Hiroko Sugimura handed across the silk ligature mounted on a long curved clamp while Sakaguchi eased traction back half an inch to open the space behind the duct; Mido passed the tie cleanly flush to the gallbladder side and doubly ligated, and Sakaguchi's suture scissors came down at the exact tail length above the knot, dividing it with a crisp snip.
nodes.em1_109: Both the cystic duct and cystic artery were securely ligated and divided in turn, leaving the operative field spotless without a trace of collateral trauma.
nodes.em1_110: Looking down at the two neat knots, Emiko Mido murmured two words almost beneath hearing:
nodes.em1_112: Keeping his retractor rock-steady, Ryuji Sakaguchi asked casually:
nodes.em1_113: "Was that a compliment for your first assistant just now?"
nodes.em1_114: "I meant the suture tail length wasn't in the way. Don't slacken your hand—we're taking the gallbladder off the liver bed subserosally."
nodes.em1_115: As dissection proceeded upward along the loose areolar plane of the hepatic gallbladder bed, visceral traction reflex made the quiet, cooperative woman behind the head drape draw a sudden breath, her voice tightening with discomfort:
nodes.em1_116: "Dr. Mido... it felt like something pulled pretty hard inside just now, and the pit of my stomach feels dull and heavy..."
nodes.em1_117: Emiko Mido immediately eased the pace of her electrocautery dissection by half a beat—offering no brush-off, just an accurate medical explanation:
nodes.em1_118: "We're separating the gallbladder from the surface of the liver right now. Epidural anesthesia blocks pain at the incision, so a dull, heavy sensation from visceral nerves under traction is normal. Tell me immediately if you feel nauseated or short of breath."
nodes.em1_119: "N-no nausea, just a little tight... will it take much longer?"
nodes.em1_120: "The critical ducts are already taken care of. Just a short stretch left."
nodes.em1_121: At the head end, Moe Honjo checked the heart rate and blood pressure readings at once and leaned down to reassure her softly:
nodes.em1_122: "Your blood pressure and heart rate are both super steady! The hardest part is already smoothly behind us—just breathe out slowly with my count and hang in there a tiny bit longer."
nodes.em1_123: Letting out a breath, the patient gripped the sheet at her sides and—out of instinctive curiosity and unease—lifted her chin an inch, as though trying to peek over the ether screen across her chest.
nodes.em1_124: Catching the motion in her peripheral vision without looking up from the serosa, Mido stopped her cold:
nodes.em1_126: "Ah... I just wanted a quick look..."
nodes.em1_127: "The sterile field in front of you isn't a viewing gallery. Lie flat."
nodes.em1_128: Moe Honjo (hurriedly dabbing the light sweat at the patient's temple with warm, damp gauze):
nodes.em1_129: "Lie nice and flat, okay? Lifting your head makes it easy to brush the sterile drape, and straining your neck tenses your abdomen too. I'm right here keeping you company."
nodes.em1_130: The patient obediently settled her head back down.
nodes.em1_131: As Sakaguchi gently elevated the inferior liver margin in concert, Mido carried the dissection through the mid-portion of the gallbladder bed. The instant the last veil of fibrous membrane parted, a slender vein coursing cleanly across the loose fascia of the gallbladder bed came into full view—so neatly laid out that a single clamp would achieve a completely bloodless plane without any hunting around.
nodes.em1_132: The bright glare of the shadowless lamp reflected in Emiko Mido's pupils above her mask.
nodes.em1_133: In that fraction of a second, the icy-cool Chief Surgeon's brow arched almost imperceptibly—like someone spotting an exquisitely crafted structure tailored to her taste—and three low words slipped out of her almost involuntarily:
nodes.em1_135: In an operating room filled otherwise only with the steady cadence of the monitor, that quiet murmur tinged with genuine pleasure carried with startling clarity.
nodes.em1_136: At the head of the table, Moe Honjo's pen froze mid-stroke on the nursing record as she looked up toward the field in mild bewilderment; beside the Mayo stand, Hiroko Sugimura merely blinked as if long used to it and wordlessly handed over a mosquito clamp.
nodes.em1_137: Behind the curtain, the patient had clearly overheard the murmur too, her voice turning hesitant and uncertain:
nodes.em1_139: Emiko Mido (clamping and ligating the small vein with brisk precision):
nodes.em1_140: "What is it—did that hurt just now?"
nodes.em1_141: "N-no, it didn't hurt... it's just, from the way you sounded a second ago... Dr. Mido, do you... really enjoy performing surgery?"
nodes.em1_142: At the head end, Moe Honjo held her breath.
nodes.em1_143: Snipping the final strand of serosal attachment, Emiko Mido placed the intact excised gallbladder steadily into the sterile kidney basin Hiroko Sugimura held out, answering without half a second's hesitation:
nodes.em1_145: "...So there really are doctors who'll admit that out loud right beside the operating table."
nodes.em1_146: "What's wrong with liking one's work? Compared to having someone stand here with a scalpel wishing they could clock out early, that ought to reassure you."
nodes.em1_147: Unable to help herself at the head end, Moe Honjo let out a soft breath, her eyes curving into a smile as she whispered to the patient:
nodes.em1_148: "That really is true... Dr. Mido gives every case her absolute all whenever she's at the table."
nodes.em1_149: After a beat of silence behind the drape came the patient's quiet reply, half nervous and half amused despite herself:
nodes.em1_150: "...Somehow it still sounds a tiny bit intimidating, though... well then, I'll leave the rest to you, Dr. Mido."
nodes.em1_151: Warm normal saline irrigated the gallbladder bed spotless. Together, the two surgeons verified that the cystic duct and arterial stumps were securely tied with zero bile leakage around the porta hepatis, leaving only two pinpoint capillary bleeders along the lower margin of the gallbladder bed before removing the protective laparotomy pad and closing the incision layer by layer.
nodes.em1_152: Setting down her suction tip, Emiko Mido stepped half a pace back and to the side on her own initiative to yield the primary operating spot, her cool, focused gaze remaining locked on the incision:
nodes.em1_153: "This last part is yours. Secure those two fine oozing points along the lower rim of the gallbladder bed, withdraw the protective pad and recheck the field, then close the incision layer by layer from peritoneum to skin."
nodes.em1_154: Clear margins, controlled risk—yet the exact closing test that laid bare a surgeon's foundational craft and hand endurance at a single glance.
nodes.em1_155: Dispensing with idle remarks, Ryuji Sakaguchi took the electrocautery forceps from Hiroko Sugimura's palm and touched the lower margin of the gallbladder bed twice with a level wrist, sealing both pinpoint bleeders cleanly without leaving a shred of excess eschar.
nodes.em1_156: Half a step back with both hands held properly within the sterile zone before her chest, Mido watched his opening move with cool eyes.
nodes.em1_158: "Once I'm done, what score are you planning to give today's test, Chief Mido?"
nodes.em1_159: Mido shot him a cool sidelong glance:
nodes.em1_160: "Run your sutures to the end before bargaining for a grade."
nodes.em1_161: Sakaguchi smiled faintly, his hands all business as he took the electrocautery forceps and sealed both pinpoint bleeders along the lower rim of the gallbladder bed with crisp precision.
nodes.em1_162: "Looks like today's 'test' has finally reached the part where I hand in my paper."
nodes.em1_163: "Let your hand tremor once before handing it in, and none of your earlier teamwork counts."
nodes.em1_164: Unruffled, Sakaguchi took the electrocautery forceps and cleanly sealed the two fine oozing points along the lower margin of the gallbladder bed.
nodes.em1_165: After verifying once more that the gallbladder bed was completely dry, Ryuji Sakaguchi steadily withdrew the warm saline laparotomy pad packing off the duodenum and transverse colon beneath the liver, returned it to the Mayo count zone, and inspected the subhepatic space and deep wound alongside Mido to confirm a clean peritoneal cavity with zero retained items.
nodes.em1_166: "Pre-closure count—abdominal protective pad removed; laparotomy pads, peanut sponges, needles, and all instruments dual-verified with Nurse Honjo. Count is correct."
nodes.em1_168: With the count confirmed, Sakaguchi took the needle holder and began abdominal closure under Emiko Mido's close, uncompromising scrutiny—running a continuous absorbable suture to close the peritoneum first, then placing interrupted stitches along the anterior rectus sheath. His wrist held a level axis throughout, bite spacing symmetrical and knot tension spot-on, earning a warm, approving look even from Hiroko Sugimura as she passed sutures beside him.
nodes.em1_169: Standing half a step back without intervening once, Mido tacitly let him approximate the subcutaneous layer and carry closure through the skin incision. Just as the final two skin stitches came through, the scrub and circulating sides completed the final verification prior to closing the wound:
nodes.em1_170: "Final end-of-case count—sponges, needles, and instruments all correct."
nodes.em1_171: "Circulating final check matches—count is completely correct!"
nodes.em1_172: Ryuji Sakaguchi squared the final skin knot, snipped the tail cleanly, smoothed a sterile dressing flat across the right subcostal incision, and only then looked up at the Chief Surgeon who had proctored him to the end.
nodes.em1_173: Emiko Mido ran her eyes over the evenly spaced dressing and spoke three cool words:
nodes.em1_176: "Eighty-five? Here I thought neither the exposure around the neck nor the closure slipped up—grading that strictly?"
nodes.em1_177: "Your judgment didn't err, and your hands are steady enough. The fifteen points off are because you spent the first five minutes feeling out my instrument tempo, and a routine elective cholecystectomy doesn't test where your floor lies on a truly complex major case."
nodes.em1_178: She paused half a second, adding as if it went without saying:
nodes.em1_179: "Besides, anyone who hands out a perfect score the first time either has standards that are too low, or has no intention of a next time."
nodes.em1_180: Sakaguchi caught the subtext beneath the cool remark:
nodes.em1_181: "Meaning there will be a next time?"
nodes.em1_182: Without rising to that directly, Mido turned toward the head of the table and issued a crisp order:
nodes.em1_183: "Surgery complete. Honjo, recheck vital signs and prepare to transfer the patient back to the ward."
nodes.em1_184: "Yes! Thank you for your hard work, doctors!"
nodes.em1_185: After carefully verifying the patient's stable blood pressure and epidural catheter dressing, Moe Honjo wheeled the thoroughly relieved, profusely grateful woman out of the operating room; Hiroko Sugimura likewise bagged the gallbladder pathology specimen, tidied the case cart, and wheeled it out ahead with a warm nod to both surgeons.
nodes.em1_186: Spacious Operating Room 1 soon fell quiet, leaving only the low, even hum of the ventilation system.
nodes.em1_187: Washing his hands clean, Ryuji Sakaguchi glanced toward Emiko Mido, who still stood unmoving before the recording desk.
nodes.em1_192: She raised her hands to untie the strings and remove her surgical mask, her motion as steady and economical as ever.
nodes.em1_193: Yet in the instant she turned her profile toward the lingering glow of the shadowless lamp, Ryuji Sakaguchi's steps slowed as he noticed an unexpected detail up close for the first time—
nodes.em1_194: Her eyes were far brighter than before the operation began.
nodes.em1_195: Those eyes—ordinarily cool to the point of indifference in her office—now shone with a sharp, incandescent brilliance, as though kindled all the way through by the dozens of exact steps just completed, the palest flush coloring the edge of her porcelain cheek.
nodes.em1_196: "You don't look remotely like someone who just stood through an open abdominal case."
nodes.em1_197: "What am I supposed to look like?"
nodes.em1_199: Lowering her lashes to pick up her fountain pen, Emiko Mido answered in a low, level voice—every word unguarded and matter-of-fact:
nodes.em1_200: "Some people feel exhilarated after a run."
nodes.em1_201: "Some people feel exhilarated after a drink."
nodes.em1_203: Her breathing seemed a fraction quicker than usual, and her fingertips rested against the rim of the metal chart board with a trace of unspent tension—yet it lasted scarcely an instant before her formidable self-control pressed everything back beneath her customary frost.
nodes.em1_204: "You may go, Dr. Sakaguchi. Today's first assistant... wasn't a waste of my time."
nodes.em1_207: Ryuji Sakaguchi stepped out of the operating room as the heavy sensor door glided shut behind him.
nodes.em1_208: Glancing back once through the glass observation window along the corridor—half the shadowless lamp now switched off, Emiko Mido standing alone beside the cool operating table writing her note—an odd intuition crossed Sakaguchi's mind:
nodes.em1_209: The Chief Surgeon hadn't gradually cooled down once the operation ended.
nodes.em1_210: On the contrary, she didn't seem to have come down from some extraordinarily heightened state yet at all.
